Why relative luminance determines contrast

Text and background contrast uses relative luminance, not raw differences between HEX numbers.

Vijeron · Updated 10 October 2026

Transform channels before weighting

In the WCAG formula, sRGB channels are normalized to 0–1 and linearized. Small channel values are divided by 12.92; other values use a 2.4 power. Relative luminance combines linear red, green and blue with weights 0.2126, 0.7152 and 0.0722.

Compare two luminances

Contrast ratio is (lighter luminance + 0.05) divided by (darker luminance + 0.05). Use full precision for the decision and round only the display. Reversing the colors does not change the ratio.

Inspect real context

The mathematical ratio helps assess solid color pairs. Photos, gradients, transparency, shadows and layers behind text require checking the effective background wherever the text appears.

Reproducible example

Black #000000 on white #FFFFFF has a 21:1 ratio. Reversing text and background remains 21:1.

What to check

Do not subtract RGB channel values and call the difference a WCAG contrast ratio.
